title: React Module 06 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of controlled and uncontrolled components, multiple inputs, validation, submit flows, async errors, and form libraries.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a controlled input in React?

options.text: An input whose value is driven by React state
An input that cannot be edited
An input controlled only by CSS
A file input with no ref

questions.explanation: Controlled inputs use React state as the source of truth and update via events.

questions.prompt: Which pair is typical for a controlled text input?
questions.explanation: A controlled text input renders `value` from state and updates state in `onChange`.

questions.prompt: Uncontrolled inputs can be read with refs or `FormData` instead of storing every keystroke in React state.
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled inputs keep their current value in the DOM and can be read when needed.

questions.prompt: Which cases often fit uncontrolled form patterns? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Simple forms read only on submit
Fields needing live validation on each keystroke

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled patterns can be useful for simple submit reads, file inputs, and DOM-oriented integrations.

questions.prompt: How can multiple related text inputs be stored in one state object?

options.text: Use one hard-coded value for every input
Store all values in a CSS class

questions.explanation: The input `name` can choose which state field to update.

questions.prompt: Why track touched state in validation?

options.text: To avoid showing errors before a user interacts with a field

questions.explanation: Touched state helps display validation feedback at a useful time.

questions.prompt: Which are valid parts of a robust submit flow? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Allow unlimited duplicate submits while pending

questions.explanation: Good submit flows prevent reloads, communicate progress, and handle errors while avoiding duplicate actions.

questions.prompt: When might a form library help?

options.text: When forms have many fields, validation rules, and repeated patterns
Only for one text input with no validation
Only when React state is forbidden
When you want to avoid accessibility concerns

questions.explanation: Libraries help manage complexity, but simple forms may not need one.
